Notice.DsnActive: Dicer is inactive while Dice So Nice is enabled. Disable one of them.
Notice.Stale: Your browser is still running an old copy of Dicer, so some of its windows may not open. Hard-reload this page (Ctrl+Shift+R, or Cmd+Shift+R on a Mac) or clear this site's cached files.
Notice.Migrated: Your Dice So Nice dice colours were imported into Dicer.
Notice.SavesImported: {n} of your saved Dice So Nice looks are now in My themes.

enabled.Name: Enable 3D dice
enabled.Hint: Throw 3D dice for chat rolls on this client.

diceLookButton.Name: Dice look button on actor sheets
diceLookButton.Hint: Show a Dice look button in the header of the sheets of actors you own; it opens the theme browser for that actor.

pixelRatioCap.Name: Pixel ratio cap
pixelRatioCap.Hint: Upper limit for the dice canvas pixel ratio. Lower is faster. Requires a reload.

diceScale.Name: Dice size
diceScale.Hint: Size of the dice on screen.

petScale.Name: Pet size
petScale.Hint: Size of the dice pets on screen, independent of the dice size.

diceAboveWindows.Name: Dice above windows
diceAboveWindows.Hint: Draw the dice over open windows and character sheets. "My rolls" lifts them only while one of your own rolls is on screen; other players' dice stay under your windows (when both show at once, all dice are lifted).

diceLighting.Name: Dice lighting
diceLighting.Hint: How your dice are lit. Studio: a bright photo studio, so every look reads clearly. Scene light: the dice take the scene's light, darker at night and coloured by its daylight or darkness. Sunlight: warm, low sunlight.

diceLight.Name: Coloured light from dice
diceLight.Hint: Clear dice pass light in their colour onto the table, and glowing dice light it in their glow colour. Applies to the next roll.

trayMode.Name: Dice tray (where your dice land)
trayMode.Hint: Where your dice land on this screen: in the GM's table tray, in your own tray (set its look in the Dice tray window), or on the scene's roll area with no tray. Drag the tray's rim to move it and its corner to resize it.

trayShow.Name: Show the dice tray
trayShow.Hint: Always on the table, or only while dice are rolling (it slides in and out).

petTray.Name: Pets and the dice tray
petTray.Hint: Where your dice pets go when there is a dice tray. On the rim, they sit on its top edge, out of the dice’s way: they still react to every roll, and a die hitting the wall beside them makes them wobble.

Choices.in: In the tray (the dice can hit them)
Choices.away: In the roll area, not the tray

trayEditor.Name: Dice tray
trayEditor.Label: Dice tray
trayEditor.Hint: The look of your dice tray: its surface, rim, corners and a design on its floor. A GM also sets the table tray here.

physicalDice.Name: Rolls from physical dice
physicalDice.Hint: Rolls whose dice came from physical dice (Pixels or another electronic dice module, or typed in by hand): animate them like any roll, also mark their chat card, or only mark the card and skip the 3D dice (a roll that mixes physical and virtual dice is still animated).

timeBeforeHide.Name: Time before hiding (ms)
timeBeforeHide.Hint: How long the dice stay on the table after landing, before they fade out.

grabDice.Name: Grab and toss landed dice
grabDice.Hint: Pick up a landed die with the mouse, drag it and fling it across the table. Only on your screen and just for fun: the result never changes, and the dice stay while you play with them.

maxDice.Name: Maximum dice per message
maxDice.Hint: Dice beyond this number are not thrown.

theme.Name: Dice theme
theme.Hint: The look and impact sound of your dice. Other players see your dice in this theme too.

worldDefaultTheme.Name: World default theme
worldDefaultTheme.Hint: The theme players' dice use when they have not chosen one of their own. Players keep their own choices unless 'Lock player looks' is on; the theme browser can also push it to every player.

lockPlayerLooks.Name: Lock player looks
lockPlayerLooks.Hint: Players' dice always use the world default theme, whatever they have chosen. Needs a world default theme. GMs are not affected, and a roll or damage type that names its own colorset or theme still does.

quality.Name: Graphics quality
quality.Hint: Auto measures your GPU once and picks a tier. Lower tiers are faster; the world cap still applies. If rolls stutter, Dicer lowers the tier for this session; choosing a quality here tries again at your choice.

showGhostDice.Name: Show ghost dice for hidden rolls
showGhostDice.Hint: Players see neutral, blank dice when a whispered roll or their own blind roll is hidden from them. This reveals that a hidden roll happened, never its result.

themedGhostDice.Name: Themed ghost dice
themedGhostDice.Hint: Ghost dice wear the roller's own dice look instead of neutral grey. Their numbers stay blank, and the look never follows the actor or the damage type, but it does show who rolled. Needs "Show ghost dice for hidden rolls".

migrateFromDsn.Name: Import Dice So Nice settings
migrateFromDsn.Hint: On first load, copy each user's Dice So Nice dice colours and the world's Dice So Nice settings into Dicer. Choices already made in Dicer are kept.

dsnReport.Name: Dice So Nice migration report
dsnReport.Label: Open the report
dsnReport.Hint: What was copied from Dice So Nice, what was kept, and which players have not migrated yet. Read-only.

hideInitiative.Name: Hide initiative until the dice land
hideInitiative.Hint: In the combat tracker, a combatant's rolled initiative stays hidden until the dice of its initiative roll have landed. When chat messages are shown immediately, the tracker shows the value at once too, as the chat card already does.

showExtraDice.Name: Show extra dice
showExtraDice.Hint: Also throw dice whose results do not count, such as the dropped die of an advantage roll or rerolled dice.

petsAllowed.Name: Allow dice pets
petsAllowed.Hint: Players' pets hop in to throw their dice and react to a natural 20 or 1.

showPets.Name: Show dice pets
showPets.Hint: See your own and other players' pets when they roll.

showOthersPets.Name: Show other players' pets
showOthersPets.Hint: Off: only your own pet comes to your rolls. Other players' pets stay off your screen, and any already resting leave.

petSounds.Name: Pet sounds
petSounds.Hint: The pets' voices: their oohs, cheers and sulks, and their reactions.

petVolume.Name: Pet sound volume
petVolume.Hint: How loud the pets are on your screen, on top of the sound effects volume.

petStay.Name: How long pets stay
petStay.Hint: How long a pet stays on the table after its owner's last roll.

petSplat.Name: Dice can splat pets
petSplat.Hint: A d20 (a check or attack, never a damage die) that hits a pet hard enough splats it until its owner rolls again; other dice only knock it about.

petView.Name: Pet view
petView.Hint: How you see pets on the table: from above like the dice, or leaning toward you so you see their faces and bodies. Only on this screen; the dice don't change.

petRestSpot.Name: Where pets rest
petRestSpot.Hint: Where your pets wait after a roll: near the dice, or wherever you last dragged a resting pet (with Click to pet on, drag one anywhere and drop it).

petClick.Name: Click to pet
petClick.Hint: Click a pet to pet it, or drag it to where your pets should rest.

petElemental.Name: Pet reactions to elemental dice
petElemental.Hint: Resting pets react to dice that land next to them: fire and lava make them fan away smoke, frost makes them shiver, storm makes them bristle, and every other element or damage type (slashing, piercing and bludgeoning included) makes them jump.

petMoods.Name: Pet moods
petMoods.Hint: Pets show a mood after high and low rolls.

petCheer.Name: Pets cheer for others
petCheer.Hint: Your pets cheer when other players roll well.

handRollTypes.Name: Dice rolled by hand
handRollTypes.Hint: The dice types Dicer sets to its method for you (console only). None chosen: all, unless you set dice to Dicer in Foundry's Dice settings yourself.

handRollsAllowed.Name: Who may roll by hand
handRollsAllowed.Hint: Players who may throw their own dice. Everyone else's dice roll automatically.

handRollsRequired.Name: Require rolling by hand
handRollsRequired.Hint: Players allowed to roll by hand always do, whatever they chose under Roll filters. A kind of roll the world default there sets to Off is exempt.

handRollTimeout.Name: Hand roll time limit (seconds)
handRollTimeout.Hint: How long a player has to throw. After that the dice roll automatically.

handReplay.Name: Replay hand throws
handReplay.Hint: Show other players' hand throws exactly as they threw them. Off shows a normal throw of the same result.

handFollowUps.Name: Throw follow-up rolls automatically
handFollowUps.Hint: A roll that starts within 3 seconds of your hand throw landing (a flat check, an automatic damage roll) is thrown for you, with no second throw screen. Also applies when the GM requires hand rolls.

handLiveShare.Name: Share hand throws live
handLiveShare.Hint: Other players see a hand throw almost as it is thrown, instead of after the thrower's dice land. The thrower's own chat card still waits for their dice. Off sends the throw once it has landed.

elementalDamageInsides.Name: Elemental damage dice
elementalDamageInsides.Hint: Fire, cold and electricity damage dice get flame, frost and storm insides instead of resin ones. Off keeps the resin look. A damage type remapped to a colorset or your own theme is not affected.

diceTray.Name: Throw by hand tool
diceTray.Hint: A button under the token controls that opens a dice picker, to throw dice by hand for a free roll.

chatTray.Name: Chat dice bar
chatTray.Hint: A row of dice under the chat box for building a roll (not the dice tray your dice land in): click a die to add it, right-click to remove it, hold for more, then Roll. Where you may roll by hand, drag dice onto the table to throw them. Hidden while another module's dice tray is on (Dice Tray, PF2e HUD).

immediatelyDisplayChatMessages.Name: Show chat messages immediately
immediatelyDisplayChatMessages.Hint: Roll messages appear in the chat at once instead of waiting for the dice to land. The dice still animate.

qualityCap.Name: Maximum graphics quality
qualityCap.Hint: Upper limit on the dice quality tier for every player in this world.

interiors.Name: Dice interiors
interiors.Hint: Draw the liquid, glitter, swirl and nebula interiors of resin dice. Off is faster.

insideMotion.Name: Living insides
insideMotion.Hint: The insides of resin dice move: liquid sloshes as the die tumbles and settles about 10 seconds after it lands. Off keeps them still, whatever each look says.

engraving.Name: Engraved numbers
engraving.Hint: Shade the numbers as engraved into the die. Off draws them flat.

shadows.Name: Dice shadows
shadows.Hint: Draw a soft shadow under each die.

glow.Name: Dice glow
glow.Hint: Let glowing looks emit light. Off keeps them unlit.

presetFaces.Name: Picture and symbol faces
presetFaces.Hint: Draw the pictures and symbols that dice presets from other modules put on their faces. Off shows plain numbers instead.

presetModels.Name: 3D model dice
presetModels.Hint: Show the 3D dice models that dice presets from other modules provide, for the die types whose face layout Dicer has verified. Off shows Dicer's own dice instead.

sounds.Name: Dice sounds
sounds.Hint: Play impact sounds as the dice hit the table, the walls and each other.

effectSounds.Name: Theme and effect sounds
effectSounds.Hint: Play the sounds themes and triggers add to results (the zap, chime, fanfare and so on). Dice impacts and pet sounds have their own settings.

soundVolume.Name: Dice sound volume
soundVolume.Hint: How loud the impact sounds are.

effectsVolume.Name: Effects volume
effectsVolume.Hint: How loud the sounds of special effects and results are.

quietWhenUnfocused.Name: Quieter when the window is unfocused
quietWhenUnfocused.Hint: Lower the dice sounds while this browser tab or window is not focused.

soundSurface.Name: Table surface
soundSurface.Hint: What the dice land on, for every player in this world. Players can override it for themselves.

soundSurfaceOverride.Name: My table surface
soundSurfaceOverride.Hint: Hear a different surface than the world's setting.

muteCoreDiceSound.Name: Silence Foundry's dice sound
muteCoreDiceSound.Hint: Foundry plays its own dice clatter on every roll card. Dicer's dice make their own sounds, so turn this off only if you want both.

effects.Name: Special effects
effects.Hint: Play effects and result sounds when a die shows a triggering result, such as a natural 20. Effects never play for rolls you cannot see.

showOthersEffects.Name: Show other players' effects
showOthersEffects.Hint: Also play the effects of other players' rolls. Off plays only the effects of your own rolls.

slowMotion.Name: Slow motion
slowMotion.Hint: Slow the landing down on this screen when a die celebrates or fumbles. Other players' timing is never affected.

screenShake.Name: Screen shake
screenShake.Hint: Let effects shake the dice briefly. Only the dice move, never the map. Off when your system asks for reduced motion.

impactEffects.Name: Impact effects
impactEffects.Hint: A few sparks where dice hit the table hard.

elementalTrails.Name: Elemental trails
elementalTrails.Hint: Dice with an elemental inside, or rolled for an elemental damage type such as fire or cold, leave a trail of that element as they fly.

elementalCritBursts.Name: Elemental critical bursts
elementalCritBursts.Hint: A natural 20 on an elemental d20 ends in a burst of that element, on any roll: attacks, saves, checks and damage.

jb2aEffects.Name: Use JB2A animations
jb2aEffects.Hint: Play JB2A's animated effects (Jules & Ben's Animated Assets) at the dice instead of the built-in ones, when the JB2A module is installed and active. Does nothing without JB2A.

insideFlare.Name: Effects flare insides
insideFlare.Hint: Crit and fumble effects reach into a resin die's inside: liquid boils, glitter scatters, fire roars, storms strike, frost flashes, the others brighten. Needs Living insides on.

perPlayerAreas.Name: Per-player roll areas
perPlayerAreas.Hint: Throw each player's dice in the area the GM gave them, on every screen. Off throws everyone's dice in the default area.

areaScale.Name: Roll area size
areaScale.Hint: Make every roll area bigger or smaller on this screen only, around its centre. Other players' screens are not affected.

gmPrivateCorner.Name: GM private corner
gmPrivateCorner.Hint: On the GM's screen, throw rolls only GMs can see (blind or GM-only whispers) in their own corner. Players' screens are never affected.

rollAreaEditor.Name: Roll areas
rollAreaEditor.Label: Edit roll areas
rollAreaEditor.Hint: Choose where dice land: a default area, one for each player and an optional GM private corner. Players can only preview their own area.

benchmark.Name: Dice benchmark
benchmark.Label: Run the dice benchmark
benchmark.Hint: Throws a few test rolls on this screen only and shows how smoothly they run. Nothing is posted to chat or sent anywhere.

damagePresets.Name: Damage dice themes
damagePresets.Hint: Give damage dice a look, impact sound and landing effect by damage type (fire, cold, acid and so on). Off shows your own dice. Never depends on the special effects setting.

damageOverDiceSet.Name: Damage dice over your dice set
damageOverDiceSet.Hint: When your dice are a module dice set (3D models or picture faces), damage dice set it aside and show their damage look. Off: damage dice keep the set's models and faces, which hide most of the damage colours.

damageMap.Name: Damage type map
damageMap.Label: Edit damage dice themes
damageMap.Hint: Choose the look, colors and landing sound of each damage type's dice. Everyone can set their own override; the GM sets the world choices.

themeBrowser.Name: Theme browser
themeBrowser.Label: Browse dice themes
themeBrowser.Hint: Browse built-in, world and your own dice themes with live previews, use one as your default, for a die type, a roll type, one of your characters or a damage type, and duplicate, edit, import or export your own. A GM can also publish themes to the world.

appearanceEditor.Name: Appearance editor
appearanceEditor.Label: Design your dice
appearanceEditor.Hint: Build a dice look layer by layer (body, inside, numbers and font, edges, glow, a look per die type) with a live turning preview, and save it as one of your themes. A GM can also save it as a world theme.

triggerEditor.Name: Trigger rules
triggerEditor.Label: Edit trigger rules
triggerEditor.Hint: Choose which effects, sounds and macros fire for which dice results. Everyone has their own rules; the GM edits the world rules.

triggerMacros.Name: Trigger macros
triggerMacros.Hint: Let trigger rules run a macro when they fire. The macro runs once, on the roller's client.

petWindow.Name: Your pet
petWindow.Label: Your pet
petWindow.Hint: Pick your dice pet and its colour. It is yours, not part of any dice theme, so it comes along whatever dice you roll.

rollStatsWindow.Name: Roll stats
rollStatsWindow.Label: Roll stats
rollStatsWindow.Hint: Everyone's d20 luck: how often each number came up tonight, in the last 30 days or ever, natural 20s and 1s, and who is on a hot streak.

statsTool.Name: Roll stats in the token tools
statsTool.Hint: Show a Roll stats button with the token tools on the left, to open the window in one click. Your choice only.

rollStats.Name: Keep roll stats
rollStats.Hint: Count every player's d20s for the Roll stats window. Only rolls everyone can see are shared; the GM's computer also keeps blind and private rolls, for the GM alone.

rollFilters.Name: Roll filters
rollFilters.Label: Roll filters
rollFilters.Hint: Choose which rolls you see as 3D dice, and which you roll by hand: grab, shake and throw your own dice, for all rolls or only some kinds (initiative, rolls during combat, damage, big rolls). The GM sets the world default.

physicsResults.Name: Physics decides the result
physicsResults.Hint: Your dice decide your rolls: each roll is thrown for you, and the faces the physics lands up are the result, instead of Foundry picking the numbers and the dice turning to show them. It takes a few milliseconds, so nothing waits for the dice, and everyone sees the same throw. Throwing by hand is always decided by the physics. Not used while the GM requires rolling by hand.

Triggers.Title: Dicer trigger rules
Triggers.WorldHint: World rules apply to every player's rolls. Module rules come from other modules and can be switched off, not edited.
Triggers.MineHint: Your own rules apply to your rolls, after the world rules.
Triggers.ReadOnly: Only a GM can edit the world rules. You can preview them.
Triggers.Name: Name
Triggers.ModuleRuleHint: From another module: switch it on or off here; it cannot be edited.
Triggers.NoneSelected: No rules yet. Add one to start.
Triggers.Label: Face label
Triggers.SceneHint: A crit scene plays with the die itself as soon as it stops, alongside the effect, and ends in its title card. One scene per die.
Triggers.SceneTextHint: Your own words for the scene's title card, one line in each box (up to 24 characters). Leave a box empty to keep the scene's own line.
Triggers.Macro: Drop a macro here, or paste its UUID
Triggers.MomentHint: A screen moment from Animater for everyone at the table: played once per roll from the GM's view, so a GM must be online and see the roll.
Triggers.ResetConfirm: Replace the world rules with the two defaults? Module rules are kept. Nothing is saved until you press Save.
Triggers.NotGM: Only a GM can save the world rules.
Triggers.Unreadable: Some saved trigger rules could not be read. They are kept, highlighted; fix or delete them.
Triggers.UnreadableRule: This saved rule could not be read and is kept unchanged. Delete it to remove it.
Triggers.PreviewUnavailable: Preview needs the 3D dice to be running.
Triggers.MomentWhereHint: The whole screen, where the dice landed (as the GM sees it), or on the roller’s token. Each moment offers the places it can happen.

AreaEditor.Title: Dicer roll areas
AreaEditor.GMHint: Drag the rectangle to move it and its handles to resize it. Each area keeps a minimum size and stays on screen. Save writes only the areas you changed.
AreaEditor.PlayerHint: This is where your dice land on this screen. Only the GM can change it; the Roll area size setting scales it for you.
AreaEditor.SaveFailed: Dicer: the roll area could not be saved.

Effects.PreviewOff: Effects are turned off in Dicer's settings.

Bench.Title: Dicer benchmark
Bench.Intro: Throws a few test rolls on this screen and measures how smoothly they animate. Wait for the dice to clear first. It takes under a minute.
Bench.Stopped: Stopped. The table shows the scenarios measured so far.
Bench.CopyFailed: Dicer: could not copy the summary.
Bench.Busy: Dicer: dice are still rolling or a benchmark is running. Try again when the table is clear.
Bench.Disabled: Dicer: 3D dice are turned off, so there is nothing to benchmark. Enable them first.
Bench.Private: Nothing is posted to chat or sent anywhere. The summary is only copied if you press Copy summary.
Bench.Unavailable: The dice engine is not running, so there is nothing to benchmark.

DamageMap.Title: Dicer damage type map
DamageMap.GMHint: World choices apply to everyone; your override applies to your dice only. A custom landing sound replaces the theme's own.
DamageMap.PlayerHint: Your override applies to your dice only. Only a GM can change the world choices and landing sounds.
DamageMap.Unreadable: Some stored damage map entries cannot be shown here and are kept as they are:
DamageMap.NoTheme: This damage type has no theme here, so your own dice are used.
DamageMap.PreviewUnavailable: Preview needs the 3D dice to be running.

Themes.Title: Dicer themes
Themes.ThrowHint: Roll one of each die with this theme on the table (only you see it).
Themes.SearchHint: Search by name (module dice also by module or dice set)
Themes.UseAsWorldDefaultHint: Every player who has not picked dice of their own rolls this theme
Themes.ClearWorldDefaultHint: No world default: players without dice of their own roll Dicer's default dice
Themes.WorldDefaultSet: This theme is now the world default.
Themes.WorldDefaultCleared: The world has no default theme now.
Themes.ClearHint: Stop using any theme choice for the selected place
Themes.StoredUnusable: Dicer could not read the stored data, so it was left unchanged. Fix or reset it in the settings first.
Themes.NotAllowed: That is not possible here (you may not own that character, or only a GM can do it).
Themes.NothingToExport: You have no themes of your own to export.
Themes.DsnFileEmpty: This Dice So Nice file has no dice Dicer can use.
Themes.ImportFailed: The theme file could not be imported.
Themes.Locked: Your GM has set everyone's dice.
Themes.PushHint: Make this every player's default theme (GM)
Themes.PushConfirm: Make this every player's default theme:
Themes.PushReplaceAll: Replace everything: also clear their per-die-type and per-roll-type choices
Themes.PushNotShared: Only built-in and world themes can be pushed: players cannot see your own themes. Publish it to the world first.
Themes.ConfirmDeleteWorldDefault: It is the world default theme: deleting it also clears the world default, and players go back to their own default dice.
Themes.Unreadable: Some stored themes cannot be read by this version and are kept as they are:

Module.Colorset: A colour set another module added (Dice So Nice API).
Module.System: A dice set another module added (Dice So Nice API). Its faces and models are used on top of your look; dice it gives no colours keep yours.
Module.MoonDiceHint: On: your default dice become the set of whichever moon has the most influence in Ember's sky right now, and change as the moons move. With no moon up you roll your own default. Dice you chose for an actor or a kind of roll stay as they are.
Module.SetFx: Play this set's own natural 20 / natural 1 effects
Module.SetFxHint: On: your d20s from this set play its own effects on a natural 20 and a natural 1, in place of the world's and your theme's. Off: they play those instead.
Module.ImportHint: Copy its colours and face images into a theme of your own, to edit
Module.Dropped: Import as theme leaves out (a theme cannot hold them):
Module.KeepHint: Use the dice set itself (Use as my default) to keep them.

Themes.TrayHint: Your dice tray: its shape, surface, rim and design
Themes.InstalledDiceHint: Load dice from installed modules that are not active

Quality.Dropped: Dicer lowered the dice graphics quality for this session to keep rolls smooth.

Appearance.Title: Dicer appearance editor
Appearance.ThrowHint: Roll one of each die with this look on the table (only you see it).
Appearance.DieType: Die type shown in the preview
Appearance.DragHint: Drag to turn, double-click to reset
Appearance.PreviewUnavailable: The live preview needs the 3D dice to be running.
Appearance.ExportLook: Export this look to a file
Appearance.ImportLook: Import a look from a file

Damage.Hint: How this theme's damage dice look, per damage type: a rogue theme can give its sneak attack (precision) dice their own look. A player's own damage overrides still win on their screen; the world's choice fills the rest.
Damage.Preview: Throw a die of this damage type as this theme makes it look

Pet.Title: Pet
Pet.Hint: Your pet throws your dice and reacts to a natural 20 or 1. Everyone sees it.
Pet.NaturalHint: Each pet in its own colours (a brown owl, a green frog...) instead of the colour you pick. Picking a colour turns this off.
Pet.PitchHint: How high or low your pet sounds, on top of its own voice (a golem is deep, a mushroom squeaky). Click your resting pet to hear it.
Pet.CatchHint: When your d20 is going to land on 20, your pet dashes over and swallows it while it is still rolling, then spits it back out showing the 20 and celebrates. Everyone who sees your pet sees it.
Pet.Hidden: You have dice pets hidden (Dicer settings).

Body.LayerLinesHint: The thin bright lines across Dichroic glass. Off: smooth glass, with the same colour turn.

Inside.MotionHint: This look's inside moves. The Living insides setting turns motion off for every look.
Inside.ResinOnly: Only clear resin dice have an inside. Choose Clear resin under Body to add one.

Numbers.OutlineHint: A line around each number, in any colour, so a number can share the die's colour and still read. It works with every fill.
Numbers.OutlineInvalid: The outline colour is not a colour (use #rrggbb). No outline is drawn until it is.
Numbers.IconsHint: Only d20s show icons; every other die keeps its numbers.
Numbers.FontInvalid: That is not a usable font name or file path, so the serif is used. Font names use letters, digits, spaces and dashes; files end in .ttf, .otf, .woff or .woff2 and must be on this Foundry server (a path in its data folder, not a web address).
Numbers.FontFailed: This font could not be loaded, so the serif is shown instead. Check the name or the file.
Numbers.ContrastHint: Lightens or darkens the number colour where it would be hard to read on the die. Picking a colour turns this off, so the numbers keep the colour you chose.
Numbers.MinContrastHint: How strongly the numbers must stand out from the die (a ratio from 1.5 to 7). Auto asks for 3, a little more for thin fonts and a little less for bold numbers.
Numbers.ContrastOk: The numbers read well on this die (contrast {ratio}:1, asks for {need}:1).
Numbers.ContrastClose: The numbers read, but only just (contrast {ratio}:1, asks for {need}:1).
Numbers.ContrastAdjusted: The number colour is adjusted to {fill} so it reads on this die (asks for {need}:1).
Numbers.ContrastOff: Keep numbers readable is off, so the numbers are drawn in the colour you picked.

Glow.Hint: A soft halo of light around the numbers (Glow ink makes the ink itself shine).

PerType.Hint: Give a die type its own look. Every other die type uses the default look above.

Extras.PreviewImpact: Throw a test die to hear the impact sound (only you see it)
Extras.PreviewNatHigh: Throw a test natural 20 with this effect and sound (only you see it)
Extras.PreviewNatLow: Throw a test natural 1 with this effect and sound (only you see it)
Extras.PickAnimation: Play a JB2A animation of your choice instead (needs Use JB2A animations on)

Appearance.Name: Theme name
Appearance.SaveWorldHint: Everyone in the world can use it (GM)
Appearance.NeedName: Give the theme a name first.
Appearance.DiscardChanges: The appearance editor has unsaved changes. Discard them and open the other look?
Appearance.NotAllowed: Only a GM can save world themes, and only your own themes can be updated.
Appearance.StoredUnusable: Dicer could not read the stored themes, so nothing was saved. Fix or reset them in the settings first.
Appearance.BadLook: That is not a Dicer look (expected the JSON of one appearance).
Appearance.ClipboardUnavailable: The clipboard is not available here.

Faces.Title: Face images
Faces.Hint: Pick an image for any face of this die; the others keep their numbers. Pick another die above the preview to give it images too.
Faces.Clear: Show the number again on face
Faces.Tint: Colour the images like the numbers (for one-colour images with transparency)
Faces.NoTensDie: A d100 shows its tens die, which has no face images: pick another die above the preview.

BodyImage.Title: Body image
BodyImage.Hint: Put a picture on the die itself: a pattern or photo wrapped around it (galaxy, stone, camo, tartan), or a crest on every face. Pick a file every player can load (world or module folders, or an https link).

ModeHint.wrap: The image flows across the whole die (best for patterns and photos)
ModeHint.face: The image sits on every face, under the number (best for a symbol or crest)

BodyImage.Tint: Colour it with the body colour

Hand.Hint: Grab the dice, shake them, and flick to throw.
Hand.AskText: Throw these dice yourself, or let them roll automatically.
Hand.MarkPartial: Rolled by hand ({n} dice rolled automatically)
Hand.MarkFollow: Thrown automatically after your hand throw
Hand.MarkPhysics: The dice decided this roll: physics threw them and read the faces

Tray.Title: Throw by hand
Tray.Hint: Click a die to add it. Right-click (or −) removes one. Then throw them by hand.
Tray.NoDice: Pick at least one die to throw.

RollFilters.Title: Roll filters
RollFilters.Intro: Which rolls you see as 3D dice. A skipped roll posts its chat card at once, as with 3D dice off. Your choice wins; "Default" follows the world setting the GM picks.
RollFilters.HandIntro: Roll by hand: grab, shake and throw your own dice; the face that lands up is the result. "All rolls" sets it for every roll you make: Off, Ask each time (you choose for each roll) or Always. A kind of roll can have its own choice, which wins over "All rolls" (initiative Off while everything else is thrown, say). A roll of several kinds takes the most cautious choice made for them: Off, then Ask. A roll that is Off rolls automatically, and its 3D dice still show. Roll tables and private rolls have no choice of their own: they are recognized only after the roll. To throw only some dice, set them to "Dicer: roll by hand" in Foundry's Dice settings (Core). While the GM requires rolling by hand, every roll is thrown, except the kinds the world default sets to Off.
